risks.title: Raw material dependency and cost volatility
risks.score_rationale: Major implicit risk for tire manufacturer: raw material costs (rubber, steel) are critical. Mentioned in CGU assessment (note 2.5.1) as key factor for future cash flow estimation. Trend is stable but structural for the sector.

risks.title: Capital intensity and depreciation of production equipment
risks.score_rationale: PP&E of €10,883M (43% of assets) with annual depreciation of €1,345M. 2017 accounting estimate change on vulcanization mold useful life reflects technological obsolescence. High structural risk for manufacturing sector.

risks.title: Technological transition toward electric and autonomous mobility
risks.score_rationale: R&D of €641M (2.9% of sales) indicates significant investment. Major implicit risk: electrification reduces tire wear (regenerative braking), autonomy changes consumption profile. Emerging critical trend for the sector.

risks.title: Increased competition from Asian and Chinese manufacturers
risks.score_rationale: Gross margin of 32.5% (€7,145/€21,960) under competitive pressure. No explicit mention but implicit in pricing strategy and R&D. Stable but chronic trend for tire sector over past 15 years.

risks.title: Environmental regulation and emission standards (tire labeling)
risks.score_rationale: EU regulation on tire labeling (rolling resistance, grip, noise) impacts design and costs. Mentioned implicitly via R&D and innovation. Upward trend: standards accelerating (Euro 7, microplastics restrictions).

risks.title: Inventory management and product obsolescence
risks.score_rationale: Inventories of €4,508M (17.8% of assets) are elevated. Tire product life cycle shortening (note 2.6) increases obsolescence risk. 2017 estimate change on molds reflects this acceleration.

risks.title: Dependency on automotive OEMs and customer concentration
risks.score_rationale: Sales include OEM (original equipment) segment not detailed. Customer receivables of €3,084M suggest concentration. Stable but structural trend: OEMs impose pricing and payment terms.

risks.title: Geopolitical risks and geographic exposure (China, Russia, USA)
risks.score_rationale: Foreign exchange differences of -€532M in 2017 reflect geographic exposure. No regional breakdown but Michelin operates globally. Upward trend: US-China trade tensions, Brexit, Russia sanctions.

ai_positioning.summary: No specific information on artificial intelligence. Michelin emphasizes digitalization, agile customer-focused organization and research and development partnerships for sustainable innovation
